Blocking: none.

I found one issue in the code files, and it is blocking. I only read the code; nothing was run.

### 1. The settings copy fails when `~/.claude/settings.json` is a symlink to a file that doesn't exist yet

- **Path:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images71-p10-2/repo/images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service`, line 10
- **Added text:** `ExecStart=/bin/cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json %h/.claude/settings.json`
- **Reason:** bug
- **Blocking:** yes (wrong outcome)
- **Description:** GNU `cp` won't write through a symlink whose target is missing. It exits non-zero with "not writing through dangling symlink". The comment on line 9 says the point of `cp` is to write through a dotfiles symlink, but that only works when the target already exists. The script running next to it in the same start, `claude-pre-approval`, does handle this case: its `merge` resolves the link with `readlink -f` and creates the missing target as `{}`. The new unit has only `Before=` ordering and no `Requires=` link to the other units, so its failure is silent to them. Pre-approval and remote control start anyway.
- **Trigger:** The workspace user's `~/.claude/settings.json` points into a dotfiles checkout that has no `settings.json`, or into a checkout that doesn't exist yet when `agent-services.target` starts. One example is a dotfiles repo that ships only `claude.json`. Another is a dotfiles clone that the Coder startup script runs after the hand-off.
- **Path:** `images/coder-template/agent-services.target@Wants` → `claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` (`cp` exits non-zero) → oneshot unit fails → `claude-pre-approval.service@ExecStart` → `claude-pre-approval@merge` (creates the target as `{}`) → `claude-remote-control.service@ExecStart`
- **Outcome:**
  - `claude-default-settings.service` ends in the failed state.
  - None of the Claude default settings are applied (model, `permissions.deny`, `autoMemoryEnabled`, and so on), at every start, for as long as the link dangles.
  - With trust on, the file holds only `{"enableAllProjectMcpServers": true}`. Remote control then starts without the denied-tools list.
- **Suggested fix:** Write the resolved path, as `claude-pre-approval@merge` does. For example: `ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$(readlink -f %h/.claude/settings.json)"'`. Optionally, add a smoke case with a dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` link.

### Candidates checked that hold up (not raised)

- **Ordering:** `Before=` alone is enough. systemd treats `A Before=B` the same as `B After=A`, and the target `Wants` all three units, so they land in one start.
- **Restarts:** A target restart re-copies the defaults through `PartOf=` plus `RemainAfterExit=`. Remote control's own `Restart=always` does not re-copy them.
- **File mode and owner:** A new file is created by `dev` with mode 0644 under the user's umask. A file that already exists keeps its mode. `merge` later replaces it at 0600 when trust is on. Nothing in it is secret.
- **Smoke test coverage:**
  - Lines 89 to 94 together would catch a copy that runs after pre-approval, because the `cp` would wipe `enableAllProjectMcpServers`.
  - They also catch the user's `"model": "smoke"` surviving.
  - Line 217 covers a fresh home.
  - Line 214 is trivially true after the `rm -rf` on line 208. It is harmless.
- **Settings keys:** I couldn't check them offline. They match the repo's own `.claude/settings.json`, so I'm not flagging them.

### Dismissed findings to log for human review

- **Overwrite is deliberate:** Defaults overwrite the user's own edits, including a tracked file in their dotfiles checkout. The PR body says this is deliberate and the smoke test asserts it, so I didn't raise it.
- **ADR 0016:** It says "nothing is ever revoked". With trust off, `enableAllProjectMcpServers` is now dropped at every start. The ADR also makes the choice once, at creation, so in practice nothing changes. It's a docs and ADR concern, outside this code-only lens.
- **`context7` plugin:** It is enabled in the defaults without its marketplace being in the image, but no failing path is shown. Dismissed as speculation.
- **`dump_extra` in `smoke.sh`:** It doesn't list `claude-default-settings.service`. That only affects failure diagnostics, not correctness.

CONFIRM — the state is reachable: a persisted home can hold a `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink whose target is missing, and `claude-pre-approval`'s `merge` already handles that case by creating the target as `{}`. GNU `cp` refuses to write through a dangling destination symlink and exits non-zero. The oneshot unit then fails, and the other units are only ordered after it, not tied to it by `Requires`. Pre-approval and remote control therefore still start without the default settings.

I did not open `agent-services.target` or `claude-pre-approval.service`, so the `Wants` and ordering-only links rest on the `Before=` lines in `claude-default-settings.service` and on your path description. I also found nothing in the repo that creates dotfiles or that symlink; that is outside the repo, and the trigger is somewhat contrived.

review.body:
Getting the Claude default settings into each workspace at start, instead of baking them under the home volume, is the right approach (ADR 0012). The PR title and description match the change.

One blocking issue: when `~/.claude/settings.json` is a symlink whose target does not exist, the new unit's `cp` fails. No default settings are applied on that start, and the units after it start anyway. Details are in the inline comment.

comments.body:
**Bug (blocking):** GNU `cp` will not write through a dangling symlink. When `~/.claude/settings.json` is a link into a dotfiles checkout that has no `settings.json` yet, `cp` exits non-zero with `not writing through dangling symlink`.

- **Trigger:** the workspace user's `~/.claude/settings.json` links to a file that does not exist when `agent-services.target` starts. For example, a dotfiles repo that ships only `claude.json`. `claude-pre-approval@merge` already expects this state: it resolves the link with `readlink -f` and creates the target as `{}`.
- **Path:** `agent-services.target@Wants` → `claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` (`cp` fails, so the oneshot unit fails) → `claude-pre-approval.service`, which still starts because it is only ordered after this unit and nothing makes it require it → `claude-pre-approval@merge` creates the target as `{}` → `claude-remote-control.service` starts.
- **Outcome:** none of the Claude default settings are applied (model, `permissions.deny`, `autoMemoryEnabled`, …). With trust on, the file holds only `enableAllProjectMcpServers`, so remote control runs without the denied tools.

**Suggested fix:** write to the resolved target, the same way `merge` does. This still keeps the link:

```ini
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$(readlink -f %h/.claude/settings.json)"'
```

Consider also adding a smoke case with a dangling `~/.claude/settings.json` link.
